## LanDrop v0.2.0

This release adds batch downloads from the browser UI, refreshes the file list,
and changes how Linux and versioning are handled. The sharing model is unchanged:
point LanDrop at a folder, start the service, open the address on another device.

### Highlights

- **Batch download** — check any files and folders in the browser and download
  them as a single zip. A floating action bar shows the selection and offers
  select-all. The archive is stored uncompressed and streamed straight to the
  socket, so memory stays flat and the LAN link is the only limit.
- **Refreshed file list** — each row now has an always-visible checkbox, a
  clearer selected state, an explicit back button, and a back-to-root path.
  Tapping the checkbox or icon selects; tapping a folder name opens it.
- **Linux ships as a `.deb`** — installing it also drops in the desktop entry,
  icon and GTK/WebKit dependencies. `sudo apt install ./LanDrop-linux-amd64.deb`.
- **macOS builds retired** — the release pipeline now produces Windows and
  Linux artifacts only. The source still builds on macOS; no installer is
  published.
- **One source of truth for versions** — `build/config.yml` → `info.version`
  feeds every platform metadata file. CI checks consistency on each push and
  derives the release version from the tag, so artifacts cannot drift.

### Downloads

| Platform | File | Install |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | `LanDrop-windows-amd64.exe` | Portable — just run it |
| Linux | `LanDrop-linux-amd64.deb` | `sudo apt install ./LanDrop-linux-amd64.deb` |

On first launch, allow the firewall / local network prompt — otherwise other
devices cannot connect.

### Batch download caveats

The zip is streamed, so it has no `Content-Length`: the browser shows no
percentage and a dropped download restarts from zero. Single-file downloads are
unchanged and still support `Range` resume — use those for one large file.

Selection is capped at 20,000 items per request. Files deleted between the
listing and the download are skipped rather than failing the whole batch.

### Please read before using

**There is no authentication.** Anyone on the same subnet who knows the address
can read and write the shared folders. Use it on a network you trust, and start
with `-readonly` when sharing with devices you do not control.

Upload resume matches on **file name**, not content: re-selecting a different
file with the same name continues from the wrong offset.
